🚨 CONSUMER WARNING: MY EXPERIENCE WITH THE SAMSUNG GALAXY Z FOLD 6 — AND WHY I WILL NEVER BUY ANOTHER Z FOLD AGAIN 🚨 I will never buy another Samsung Z Fold device again. I own a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6, and after just over a year and a half of use—despite taking extremely good care of the device—the internal screen failed. Samsung quoted me more than R$6,000 (approximately US$1,000+) to repair it. For a supposedly premium smartphone that costs thousands of dollars, this is simply unacceptable. I want to share my experience as a warning to anyone considering purchasing a Samsung foldable phone. My Galaxy Z Fold 6 was in excellent physical condition. It had NO drops, NO impacts, NO cracks caused by accidents, and NO signs of misuse. Nevertheless, the device developed a serious problem with what appears to be one of the most critical components of any foldable smartphone: the internal display. The touchscreen on the main internal screen suddenly stopped working properly, and a black line/stain appeared exactly along the central folding crease. Let that sink in: the defect appeared precisely in the area that is repeatedly folded every time the device is used as designed. I acted in good faith and followed the official procedures. I sought technical assistance and expected Samsung to properly evaluate what I believe may be a latent or hidden manufacturing defect. Instead, I was faced with a repair estimate of more than R$6,000.
